l: the last day, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 36
s: Alma says those who trust in God will be lifted up at the last day. He knows that God will raise him up at the last day to dwell with him in glory.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: Helaman is commanded by his father to preserve the sacred records, plates, and interpreters, and to keep a record of the people. His father teaches him that God uses small and simple means, including records and the Liahona, to fulfill wise purposes, reveal truth, guide people, and bring souls to salvation. Helaman is instructed to keep the commandments of God, counsel with the Lord, preach repentance and faith in Jesus Christ, and teach the people to reject sin, iniquity, and the secret works of darkness. The unit also explains the preservation and restoration of the Lamanites, the destruction of wicked workers of darkness, and the symbolic relationship between the Liahona and the word of Christ.

l: Helaman, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: Helaman is commanded to preserve the sacred records, plates, twenty-four plates, and interpreters, and to keep a record of the people. He is told to keep the commandments of God, counsel with the Lord, preach repentance and faith in Jesus Christ, and teach the people to reject sin and iniquity.

l: Helaman's father, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: Helaman's father commands him to care for the sacred things entrusted to him and teaches him about their preservation and purposes. He instructs Helaman to preach, be diligent, and look to God and live.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: God preserves sacred records and works through small and simple means to fulfill eternal purposes, confound the wise, and bring about the salvation of many souls. He directs, protects, and fulfills his promises to those who keep his commandments.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: Jesus Christ is identified as the Redeemer whose knowledge brings people to rejoice and whose words guide people toward eternal bliss. Faith in Jesus Christ is taught as a defense against temptation.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: Many thousands of the Lamanites are brought to repentance and to the knowledge of the Lord their God through the records and the words of Ammon and his brethren. They are restored to the knowledge of the truth and will be preserved for future generations.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: Many Nephites are described as stiffnecked and as hardening their hearts in sin and iniquity. The records may help bring many of them to the knowledge of their Redeemer.

l: workers of darkness and secret combinations, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: Workers of darkness and secret combinations commit murders, robbings, plunderings, wickedness, and abominations. They are subject to destruction when fully ripe unless they repent.

l: promised land, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: The Liahona directs people along a straight course to the promised land. Following its course brought the fathers of the people to that land.

l: records, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: The records enlarge the memory of the people, convince many of the error of their ways, and bring them to the knowledge of God and salvation. They helped Ammon and his brethren convince many thousands of the Lamanites to repent.

l: plates of Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: The plates of Nephi contain records that are to be kept and preserved as sacred. They are part of the records entrusted to Helaman.

l: plates of brass, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: The plates of brass contain engravings, holy scriptures, and the genealogy of the forefathers. They are prophesied to be preserved and handed down until they go forth to every nation, kindred, tongue, and people.

l: twenty-four plates, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: The twenty-four plates are to be kept so that the mysteries, works of darkness, secret works, murders, robbings, plunderings, wickedness, and abominations of a destroyed people may be made manifest.

l: interpreters, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: The interpreters were prepared so that the word of God concerning the secret works and abominations of a destroyed people could be fulfilled. Helaman is commanded to preserve them.

l: Liahona, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: The Liahona is a ball or director prepared by the Lord to show the fathers the course they should travel in the wilderness. It worked according to their faith, but its marvelous works ceased when they were slothful and forgot to exercise faith and diligence.

l: commandments of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: Keeping the commandments of God leads to prosperity in the land and preserves sacred things. Transgressing them brings separation from God's presence and can cause sacred things to be taken away.

l: word of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: The word of Christ points people along a straight course to eternal bliss. Following its course can carry them beyond the vale of sorrow into a far better land of promise.

l: mysteries, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: The mysteries are not yet fully made known to Helaman's father. They are preserved for a wise purpose known to God.

l: works of darkness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: The secret works of a destroyed people, including their murders, robbings, plunderings, wickedness, and abominations, are to be made known to the people. Their oaths, covenants, agreements, signs, and wonders are to be kept from the people.

l: secret plans, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: The secret plans of oaths and covenants are to be kept from the people. The people are instead to be taught to hate sin and iniquity and to understand that the workers of darkness were destroyed for their wickedness and murders.

l: iniquity, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: Sin and iniquity cause people to harden their hearts and lead workers of darkness and secret combinations toward destruction. The people are to be taught an everlasting hatred of sin and iniquity.

l: faith in Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: Faith in God enabled the Liahona to show the way and brought about miracles. Faith in Jesus Christ helps people withstand every temptation of the devil.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: Repentance brings people to the knowledge of the Lord and is required for workers of darkness and secret combinations to avoid destruction. Helaman is commanded to preach repentance.

l: salvation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: The records and the words they contain bring people to the knowledge of God and contribute to the salvation of their souls. God works through small means to bring about the salvation of many souls.

l: conversion of the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: The restoration of many thousands of the Lamanites to the knowledge of the truth is identified as one purpose God has fulfilled. God has shown his power in them and will continue to show it in future generations.

l: destruction of the wicked, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 37
s: The wicked workers of darkness and secret combinations were destroyed after they failed to repent. The land is cursed to destruction for such workers unless they repent before they are fully ripe.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 38
s: The unit concerns counsel to Shiblon about faithfulness, obedience, teaching, humility, self-control, and enduring to the end. Shiblon is reminded that trusting God brings deliverance from trials and afflictions and that God’s commandments bring prosperity, while disobedience cuts people off from God’s presence. The speaker teaches that salvation comes only through Christ and recounts receiving remission of sins after crying to the Lord Jesus Christ for mercy. Shiblon is instructed to continue teaching the word diligently, temperately, boldly, humbly, and with love.

l: Shiblon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 38
s: Shiblon is praised for his faithfulness, diligence, patience, and long-suffering among the Zoramites. He is counseled to trust in God, continue keeping the commandments, teach the word, avoid pride and idleness, bridle his passions, and acknowledge his unworthiness before God.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 38
s: God grants prosperity to those who keep his commandments and cuts off those who do not keep them from his presence. Trust in God brings deliverance from trials, troubles, and afflictions, and the Spirit of God makes spiritual knowledge known.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 38
s: The Lord Jesus Christ is the means through which people can be saved and is the life, light, word of truth, and righteousness of the world. Crying to him for mercy brought peace to the speaker’s soul and remission of sins.

l: the Spirit of the Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 38
s: The Spirit of God is in the speaker and makes spiritual things known to him.

l: Zoramites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 38
s: The Zoramites are described as praying to be heard by people and praised for their wisdom. Shiblon is told not to pray as they do.

l: commandments of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 38
s: Keeping the commandments of God leads to prosperity in the land and continued blessing, while refusing to keep them leads to being cut off from God’s presence.

l: afflictions, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 38
s: Trials, troubles, and afflictions can be endured and overcome through trust in God. Those who trust in God will be delivered from them and lifted up at the last day.

l: remission of sins, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 38
s: Remission of sins was received after the speaker cried to the Lord Jesus Christ for mercy following three days and three nights of bitter pain and anguish of soul.

l: salvation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 38
s: Salvation is possible only in and through Christ, with no other way or means by which people can be saved.

l: word of truth and righteousness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 38
s: The word of truth and righteousness is identified with Christ, who is also described as the life and light of the world.

l: preaching of the word, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 38
s: Shiblon is instructed to continue teaching the word to the people. His teaching should be diligent, temperate, bold without overbearance, and accompanied by humility, love, and self-control.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 39
s: The speaker admonishes his son for boasting, forsaking the ministry, and following Isabel, and commands him to repent, seek counsel, and refrain from iniquity. The son is told to return to the Zoramites, acknowledge his faults, and no longer lead people toward wickedness. The unit teaches that Christ will come to take away the sins of the world and declare glad tidings of salvation. It explains that the plan of redemption is made known beforehand because souls are equally precious to God at all times.

l: Isabel, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 39
s: Isabel is described as a harlot who stole away the hearts of many. The son followed her into the land of Siron among the borders of the Lamanites.

l: Zoramites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 39
s: The Zoramites were affected by the son's conduct, and when they saw it they would not believe the speaker's words. The son is commanded to return to them and acknowledge his faults.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 39
s: God sees the son's crimes, and they will stand as a testimony against him at the last day unless he repents. God considers souls precious and sends angels to declare glad tidings.

l: Holy Ghost, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 39
s: Denying the Holy Ghost after it has had place in a person, with knowledge that it is being denied, is described as an unpardonable sin.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 39
s: Christ is the one who will come to take away the sins of the world and declare glad tidings of salvation to his people.

l: ministry, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 39
s: The son was entrusted with a ministry to declare glad tidings to the people and prepare their minds for the coming of Christ. He forsook this ministry when he went after Isabel.

l: sin, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 39
s: The son is commanded to repent and forsake his sins. Sins are described as preventing inheritance of the kingdom of God unless they are abandoned.

l: crimes, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 39
s: The son's crimes cannot be hidden from God and will testify against him at the last day unless he repents. The speaker dwells on them for the son's good.

l: wickedness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 39
s: The son brought great iniquity upon the Zoramites through his conduct. He is commanded to refrain from his iniquities and turn to the Lord with all his mind, might, and strength.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 39
s: The son is commanded to repent, forsake his sins, return to the Zoramites, and acknowledge his faults and the wrong he has done.

l: kingdom of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 39
s: The son cannot inherit the kingdom of God unless he crosses himself in the lusts of his eyes and forsakes these things.

l: glad tidings, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 39
s: Glad tidings concern the coming of Christ, who will declare salvation to his people. The son's ministry was to declare these glad tidings and prepare the people for Christ's coming.

l: salvation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 39
s: Christ will come to declare glad tidings of salvation unto his people. The ministry was intended to prepare the people so that salvation might come unto them.

l: the plan of redemption, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 39
s: The plan of redemption is to be made known to the people as well as to their children. It can be declared beforehand because souls are as precious to God before Christ's coming as afterward.

l: coming of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 39
s: The coming of Christ is the subject of the son's ministry and involves Christ taking away the sins of the world and declaring glad tidings of salvation. The people and their children are to be prepared to hear the word at the time of his coming.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: The unit concerns the resurrection and the state of men's souls between death and the appointed time of resurrection. It explains that God has appointed a time when all shall rise, though men do not know when it will be. Righteous spirits enter paradise, while wicked spirits are cast into outer darkness until resurrection. At resurrection, souls and bodies are reunited, restored to their proper and perfect frame, and brought before God for judgment according to their works.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: God appoints the time when the dead shall rise and knows all appointed times. He gives men life, receives spirits after death, and judges them according to their works.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: Christ brings to pass the resurrection of the dead. The resurrection of those who die after his resurrection occurs after his coming.

l: mankind, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: Men do not know the appointed time of resurrection, and time is measured unto them. Their spirits are taken home to God after they depart from the mortal body.

l: the righteous, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: The spirits of the righteous are received into paradise, a state of happiness, rest, and peace. The righteous are reunited with their bodies and later shine forth in the kingdom of God.

l: the wicked, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: The spirits of the wicked are cast into outer darkness because of their iniquity and their choice of evil works. They remain in misery until resurrection and are then consigned to partake of the fruits of their evil works.

l: devil, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: The devil enters into the wicked and takes possession of their house. He leads them captive by his will.

l: resurrection of the dead, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: The resurrection is the coming forth of the dead and the reuniting of soul and body. It occurs after Christ's coming, at a time appointed by God, and is followed by judgment.

l: resurrection of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: The resurrection of Christ marks the point before which the first resurrection includes those from the days of Adam. The righteous may have their souls and bodies reunited at Christ's resurrection and ascension, though the exact timing is not stated.

l: first resurrection, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: The first resurrection is described as involving the reuniting of the souls and bodies of those from the days of Adam down to the resurrection of Christ. It is not merely the consignation of souls to happiness or misery.

l: temporal death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: Death separates the soul from the body. After death, the spirit enters a state of happiness or misery while awaiting resurrection.

l: judgment, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: After souls and bodies are reunited, they are brought to stand before God and judged according to their works.

l: reuniting of soul and body, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: The reuniting of soul and body occurs at resurrection. It restores every limb, joint, and even every hair to its proper and perfect frame.

l: soul, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: The soul exists in happiness or misery between death and resurrection. At resurrection, it is restored to the body and brought before God for judgment.

l: body, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: The body remains separate from the soul between death and resurrection. At resurrection, it is reunited with the soul and restored to its proper and perfect frame.

l: paradise, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: Paradise is the state of happiness, rest, and peace where the spirits of the righteous rest from trouble, care, and sorrow before resurrection.

l: endless night of darkness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: Outer darkness is the state to which the spirits of the wicked are cast. It includes weeping, wailing, gnashing of teeth, and fearful expectation of God's wrath.

l: kingdom of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: The righteous shine forth in the kingdom of God after the restoration. No unclean thing can inherit it.

l: restoration, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: Restoration brings souls and bodies back together and restores every limb, joint, and hair to its proper and perfect frame. It fulfills what the prophets have spoken.

l: appointed time, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: God has appointed a time when all shall come forth from the dead, though no one among men knows when it will be. The appointed time includes the resurrection and the end of the interim states of happiness and misery.

l: space between death and resurrection, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 40
s: There is a space between death and the resurrection of the body. During this space, souls remain in paradise or outer darkness until God appoints the time for them to come forth.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: The speaker explains to his son that restoration is required by the justice of God and that all things will return to their proper order through the power and resurrection of Christ. Men will be restored according to their works and the desires of their hearts, receiving either good and happiness or evil and misery. The speaker teaches that wickedness cannot be restored to happiness and that restoration returns evil for evil and good for good. He urges his son to be merciful, deal justly, judge righteously, and do good continually.

l: the speaker's son, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: He is taught about the meaning of restoration and warned not to risk further offense against God. He is urged to be merciful, deal justly, judge righteously, and do good continually.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: His power and resurrection make it requisite that the soul of man be restored to its body and that every part of the body be restored to itself.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: His decrees are unalterable, and the way is prepared so that whoever will may walk therein and be saved.

l: mankind, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: They are judged according to their works and the desires of their hearts, and they are restored to good or evil according to what they have done and desired.

l: restoration, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: It brings all things back to their proper order and returns evil for evil, carnal for carnal, devilish for devilish, and good for good. It condemns the sinner and does not justify him.

l: justice, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: It requires that all things be restored to their proper order and that men be judged according to their works.

l: resurrection of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: They make possible the restoration of the soul to the body and of every part of the body to itself.

l: soul, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: It is restored to its body according to the power and resurrection of Christ.

l: body, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: Every part of it is restored to itself, and mortality is raised to immortality.

l: works, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: They determine what men are restored to at the last day. Good works result in restoration to good, while evil works result in restoration to evil.

l: desires of the heart, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: They are considered with works in determining what men are restored to at the last day.

l: never-ending happiness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: It is received according to desires of happiness and good. Wickedness never was happiness.

l: misery, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: It is the endless result for those restored to evil and who inherit the kingdom of the devil.

l: kingdom of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: It is inherited by those raised to endless happiness.

l: kingdom of the devil, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: It is inherited by those raised to endless misery.

l: sin, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: It is not removed by restoration into happiness; the speaker warns his son not to commit further sin.

l: wickedness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: It never was happiness, and restoration does not change it into happiness.

l: righteousness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: Those who repent and desire it until the end of their days are rewarded unto righteousness. It is restored to those who act righteously.

l: state of nature, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: Those in it, or in a carnal state, are in the gall of bitterness and bonds of iniquity, without God in the world.

l: nature of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: Men in a carnal state have gone contrary to it.

l: nature of happiness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: Those in a carnal state are in a state contrary to it.

l: mercy, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: It is restored to those who are merciful unto their brethren.

l: judgment, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 41
s: A righteous judgment is restored to those who judge righteously.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: The speaker explains to his son how God’s justice and mercy operate in the punishment and redemption of sinners. He teaches that Adam and our first parents were cut off from the tree of life and from the presence of the Lord, bringing temporal and spiritual death upon mankind. The probationary state gives mankind time to repent, while the atonement allows mercy to satisfy the demands of justice without destroying justice. The speaker urges his son to repent, trust God’s justice and mercy, and preach the word to bring others to repentance.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: God placed cherubim and a flaming sword to prevent man from partaking of the tree of life. God atoneth for the sins of the world, brings about mercy and resurrection, and remains both perfect, just, and merciful.

l: the speaker's son, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: The speaker's son is taught about the justice of God, the fall, repentance, mercy, and the atonement. He is called of God to preach the word with truth and soberness and bring souls unto repentance.

l: Adam, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: Adam would have lived forever without space for repentance if he had immediately partaken of the tree of life. He became subject to temporal and spiritual death after being cut off from the tree of life.

l: our first parents, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: Our first parents were sent out from the garden of Eden and were cut off from the tree of life. They became cut off temporally and spiritually from the presence of the Lord and became subject to their own will.

l: mankind, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: Mankind became fallen, carnal, sensual, and devilish by nature, and was placed in a probationary state to prepare. Mankind can be reclaimed from spiritual death through repentance and the plan of redemption, but is judged according to works, law, and justice.

l: garden of Eden, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: The garden of Eden was the place from which the Lord God sent our first parents forth to till the ground.

l: tree of life, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: The tree of life was guarded by cherubim and a flaming sword so that man could not partake of its fruit and live forever without a space for repentance.

l: the presence of the Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: The presence of the Lord is what mankind was cut off from through spiritual death. The resurrection of the dead brings men back into the presence of God to be judged.

l: the fall of man, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: The fall brought temporal and spiritual death upon all mankind. It made mankind carnal, sensual, and devilish by nature and created the need for redemption.

l: temporal death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: Temporal death came through being cut off from the tree of life and from the face of the earth. It was not expedient for man to be reclaimed from this death because that would destroy the great plan of happiness.

l: spiritual death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: Spiritual death is being cut off from the presence of the Lord. The plan of redemption provides a means for mankind to be reclaimed from it.

l: the probationary state, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: The probationary state is a time granted to man to repent and serve God. It is a preparatory state in which mankind can meet the conditions required for mercy.

l: the plan of redemption, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: The plan of salvation would have been frustrated if Adam had lived forever without a space for repentance. It concerns the redemption and salvation made possible through God’s purposes.

l: the plan of happiness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: The plan of happiness is described as eternal as the life of the soul. Reclaiming man from temporal death would destroy it.

l: redemption, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: The plan of redemption provides the means to reclaim mankind from spiritual death through repentance and the atonement. Without it, the souls of the dead would remain miserable and cut off from the Lord’s presence.

l: the plan of mercy, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: The plan of mercy could not be brought about without an atonement. Through the atonement, mercy appeases the demands of justice.

l: justice, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: Justice consigns unrepentant mankind to be cut off from God’s presence and requires the punishment affixed to the law. Justice exercises all its demands, while it cannot be robbed by mercy.

l: mercy, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: Mercy claims the penitent because of the atonement. It cannot take effect by destroying justice, and none but the truly penitent are saved.

l: the Atonement of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: The atonement is made by God himself for the sins of the world. It brings about the plan of mercy, appeases the demands of justice, and brings to pass the resurrection of the dead.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: Repentance is granted during the probationary state and is claimed by mercy. It requires sin and punishment to exist, and the speaker urges his son and others to come down to repentance.

l: sin, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: Sin brings remorse of conscience and places mankind under the claims of justice. The speaker tells his son to let his sins trouble him in a way that leads to repentance.

l: law, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: The law is given with an affixed punishment and makes sin recognizable. Justice executes the law, and the law inflicts the punishment when mercy does not claim the creature.

l: punishment, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: Punishment is affixed to the law and is eternal as the life of the soul. It makes repentance possible and is executed by the law when justice claims the sinner.

l: resurrection of the dead, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: The resurrection of the dead is brought about by the atonement. It returns men into the presence of God, where they are judged according to their works, the law, and justice.

l: salvation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: Salvation comes through God’s great and eternal purposes, including the plan of mercy and the atonement. None but the truly penitent are saved.

l: redemption of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 42
s: Redemption of men comes through the atonement and the plan of redemption. It reclaims mankind from spiritual death and is part of God’s eternal purposes.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: Alma and his sons preach the word, while the account returns to the wars between the Nephites and the Lamanites. Led by Moroni, the Nephites prepare to defend their lands, families, rights, liberty, and worship of God against Zerahemnah’s Lamanite armies, which include Amalekites and Zoramites. Alma reveals that the Lamanites are marching toward Manti, allowing Moroni to arrange an ambush near the river Sidon. The Nephites defeat and surround the more numerous Lamanite armies after praying for freedom, and Moroni commands his men to stop shedding their blood.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: Alma goes forth with his sons to declare the word. At Moroni’s request, he inquires of the Lord and learns that the Lamanites are marching through the wilderness toward Manti.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: The Nephites prepare to defend their lands, houses, wives, children, rights, privileges, liberty, and worship of God. They defeat and surround the more numerous Lamanites after crying unto the Lord for freedom.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: The Lamanites come against the Nephites with thousands under Zerahemnah. They are initially frightened by the Nephites’ armor, later fight with great strength and courage, and finally flee before the Nephites.

l: Zoramites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: The Zoramites become Lamanites and join the Lamanite armies. Their leaders serve as chief captains, and they inspire the Lamanites to fight fiercely.

l: Amalekites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: The Amalekites are described as more wicked and murderous than the Lamanites. They become chief captains under Zerahemnah and inspire the Lamanites in battle.

l: Moroni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: Moroni, appointed chief captain at twenty-five years of age, commands the Nephite armies and their wars. He uses spies, Alma’s revelation, concealed forces, and stratagem to defeat and surround the Lamanites.

l: Zerahemnah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: Zerahemnah leads the Lamanite armies and appoints Amalekites and Zoramites as chief captains to preserve hatred toward the Nephites. His forces are eventually surrounded by Moroni’s and Lehi’s armies.

l: Lehi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: Lehi leads an army concealed south of hill Riplah. He attacks the Lamanites from the rear, drives them across the river Sidon, and keeps his army on the eastern bank.

l: land of Jershon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: Jershon is where the Nephites gather their armies and where Moroni first meets the Lamanites. Moroni leaves part of his army there to guard against a Lamanite attack.

l: Antionum, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: Antionum is the land of the Zoramites. The Lamanite armies gather there under Zerahemnah before moving through the wilderness toward Manti.

l: wilderness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: The Lamanites travel through the wilderness around the head of the river Sidon to reach Manti. Moroni sends spies into the wilderness and hides part of his army there.

l: river Sidon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: The Lamanites cross the river Sidon while fleeing Lehi and Moroni. The Nephites hold both banks and use the river to encircle the Lamanite armies.

l: Manti, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: Manti is the land the Lamanites intend to possess and attack through its weaker part. Moroni marches there, gathers its people for battle, and arranges the Nephite ambush nearby.

l: war, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: The account returns to the wars between the Nephites and the Lamanites in the eighteenth year of the reign of the judges. The conflict concerns the defense of lands, families, liberty, rights, and worship of God.

l: armies of the Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: The Nephite armies are equipped with breastplates, arm-shields, head-plates, shields, thick clothing, swords, cimeters, and other weapons. Under Moroni and Lehi, they defeat, pursue, and surround the Lamanite armies.

l: armies of the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: The Lamanite armies are more than twice as numerous as the Nephites but lack comparable armor. They suffer heavy losses, flee toward the river Sidon, and are surrounded in the valley.

l: liberty, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: The Nephites fight to preserve their liberty and freedom from bondage. When they cry unto the Lord for freedom, they gain power and the Lamanites begin to flee.

l: worship at the holy stand, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: The Nephites seek to preserve the ability to worship God according to their desires. They know that the Lamanites would destroy those who worship God in spirit and in truth.

l: defense of families and lands, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 43
s: The Nephites contend to defend their families, lands, country, rights, and religion. The Lord has said that they should defend their families even unto bloodshed.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 44
s: Moroni tells Zerahemnah that the Lord has delivered the Lamanites into the Nephites’ hands because of their faith and religion, and demands that they surrender their weapons and covenant not to return to war. Zerahemnah initially refuses to take an oath, and after Moroni returns his weapons, a Nephite soldier breaks his sword and removes his scalp. Many Lamanites surrender after seeing the scalp, but Zerahemnah stirs the remainder to fight until Moroni’s forces begin killing them. Zerahemnah then promises a covenant of peace, the fighting stops, and the surviving Lamanites depart, while many Nephites and Lamanites have died.

l: Moroni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 44
s: Moroni tells Zerahemnah that the Nephites do not desire to be men of blood or bring anyone into bondage. He demands the surrender of the Lamanites’ weapons and an oath not to return to war, commands the Nephites to attack when Zerahemnah refuses, and stops the killing when Zerahemnah agrees to a covenant of peace.

l: Zerahemnah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 44
s: Zerahemnah delivers his weapons but refuses to take an oath, saying that he and his children would break it. He attacks Moroni, loses his sword and scalp, stirs the remaining Lamanites to fight, and later promises a covenant of peace to spare the survivors.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 44
s: The Nephites are delivered into the Lamanites’ hands through their faith, religion, and support from the Lord. Their armies defeat and kill many Lamanites, then return to their houses and lands.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 44
s: The Lamanites initially refuse to covenant peace and continue fighting after some surrender. Many are killed, while the remainder surrender their weapons, enter a covenant of peace, and depart into the wilderness.

l: Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 44
s: The Lord delivers the Lamanites into the Nephites’ hands and supports, keeps, and preserves the Nephites while they remain faithful. Moroni says the Lord will not suffer them to be destroyed unless they transgress and deny their faith.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 44
s: Moroni identifies the true faith as faith in God and says God will support and preserve the faithful. Zerahemnah does not believe that God delivered the Lamanites into the Nephites’ hands.

l: battle, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 44
s: The battle concerns the Nephites and Lamanites, with the Nephites gaining power and defeating the Lamanites. The fighting resumes after Zerahemnah refuses the oath and ends after he promises a covenant of peace.

l: conflict, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 44
s: Moroni says the conflict will end if the Lamanites accept his conditions. When Zerahemnah refuses, the conflict continues until the Lamanites are being destroyed.

l: war against the Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 44
s: The Lamanites came against the Nephites to make war because of their anger toward the Nephites’ religion. Moroni requires them to surrender their weapons and promise not to return to war.

l: covenant of peace, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 44
s: Many Lamanites enter into a covenant of peace and are allowed to depart into the wilderness. Zerahemnah later promises that he and his people will make the same covenant if the remaining Lamanites are spared.

l: death of the combatants, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 44
s: Many Nephites and Lamanites die, and the number of dead is not counted because it is exceedingly great. Their bodies are cast into the waters of Sidon and buried in the depths of the sea.

l: swords, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 44
s: Zerahemnah delivers his sword, cimeter, and bow to Moroni but refuses the required oath. Moroni returns the weapons, later takes the Lamanites’ weapons after their covenant, and the surrendered weapons are not retained by the departing Lamanites.

l: scalp of Zerahemnah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 44
s: A Nephite soldier removes Zerahemnah’s scalp and raises it on the point of his sword. He declares that the Lamanites will fall unless they surrender their weapons and depart with a covenant of peace, and many are frightened into surrendering.

l: faith in Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 44
s: Moroni says the Nephites have been delivered and preserved because of their faith in Christ. He says the Lamanites cannot destroy this faith and that the Nephites will be preserved while faithful.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 45
s: The people of Nephi rejoice and give thanks to the Lord after being delivered from their enemies, but Alma prophesies that they will later dwindle in unbelief, suffer wars, pestilences, famines, and bloodshed, and become extinct. Alma teaches Helaman, receives his belief in the records and in Jesus Christ, and charges him to keep the commandments and record the prophecy. Alma blesses Helaman, his other sons, the land, and the church before departing from Zarahemla and never being heard of again. Helaman and his brethren reestablish the church throughout the land, but some become proud because of their riches and refuse to heed their words.

l: people of Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 45
s: The people of Nephi rejoice because the Lord delivers them from their enemies, and they give thanks, fast, pray, and worship God. Alma prophesies that they will dwindle in unbelief, suffer wars, pestilences, famines, and bloodshed, and eventually become extinct.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 45
s: Alma teaches Helaman about the records, Jesus Christ, and keeping commandments. He prophesies concerning the future of the people of Nephi, blesses Helaman, his other sons, the land, and the church, then departs from Zarahemla and is never heard of again.

l: Helaman, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 45
s: Helaman affirms his belief in the records and in Jesus Christ and promises to keep Alma’s commandments. He later goes among the people to declare the word and, with his brethren, reestablishes the church throughout the land.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 45
s: Jesus Christ is the one whom Alma asks Helaman whether he believes will come. Alma says that Jesus Christ will manifest himself to the people of Nephi.

l: Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 45
s: The Lord delivers the people of Nephi from their enemies, and they give thanks unto him. Alma says the Lord will prosper Helaman in the land, and the church says Alma was taken up by the Spirit or buried by the hand of the Lord.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 45
s: God is worshipped by the people of Nephi with great joy. Alma teaches that God curses and blesses the land and cannot look upon sin with the least degree of allowance.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 45
s: The Lamanites will number among those remaining after the destruction of the people of Nephi, and most will become like the Lamanites. The Lamanites will pursue the few who are called the disciples of the Lord until those disciples become extinct.

l: church, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 45
s: Alma blesses the church and those who stand fast in the faith. Helaman and his brethren reestablish the church throughout the land and appoint priests and teachers, but a dissension arises and some refuse to heed their words.

l: land, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 45
s: Alma blesses the land for the righteous’ sake and says it will be cursed unto destruction for every nation, kindred, tongue, and people that do wickedly when fully ripe. The people of Nephi possess the land, where Helaman and his brethren establish churches.

l: faith in Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 45
s: Alma blesses those in the church who stand fast in the faith from that time onward.

l: prophecy, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 45
s: Alma commands Helaman to write his prophecy and not make it known until it is fulfilled. The prophecy concerns the future unbelief, destruction, and extinction of the people of Nephi and the fate of those who remain.

l: unbelief, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 45
s: Alma prophesies that the people of Nephi will dwindle in unbelief four hundred years after Jesus Christ manifests himself to them. Their unbelief will lead them into darkness, lasciviousness, and iniquities.

l: iniquity, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 45
s: Alma says the people of Nephi will fall into all manner of iniquities and sin against great light and knowledge. He says that because of iniquity the prophecy concerning their destruction will be fulfilled, and that great iniquity will arise by the fourth generation.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: Amalickiah leads dissenters who seek power and want him to be king, flattering many people away from the church and the foundation of liberty. Moroni responds by creating and proclaiming the title of liberty, gathering the people, and marching against Amalickiah’s forces. Amalickiah flees to the land of Nephi, while many of his followers are captured, returned to the land of Zarahemla, or required to covenant to support freedom. The Nephites regain peace, and Helaman and the high priests maintain order in the church.

l: Amalickiah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: Amalickiah is a large and strong man who desires to be king. Through cunning devices and flattering words, he leads many people into dissensions, wickedness, and an attempt to destroy the church of God and the foundation of liberty. He flees with some followers to the land of Nephi when Moroni’s people become more numerous.

l: Moroni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: Moroni, chief commander of the Nephite armies, becomes angry when he hears of the dissensions. He creates and proclaims the title of liberty, gathers those who want to maintain their liberty, marches against Amalickiah, captures many of his followers, and establishes the standard of liberty among the Nephites.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: God grants liberty and other blessings to the people for the righteous’ sake. Moroni prays to God for the blessings of liberty to remain with his brethren, and the people covenant with God to keep his commandments. God prepares plants and roots that remove the causes of diseases.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: Jesus Christ is the one by whom many who die firmly believing are redeemed. True believers take upon themselves the name of Christ and are happy in him when they die in faith.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: The Nephites face dangerous dissensions after their victory over the Lamanites. Many Nephites gather under Moroni, covenant to maintain their rights and religion, and restore peace in the land.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: The Lamanites have recently been defeated by the Nephites. Moroni seeks to prevent them from gaining more strength and knows that Amalickiah will stir them to anger against the Nephites.

l: Amalickiahites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: The Amalickiahites are dissenters who support Amalickiah. Many are captured and returned to the land of Zarahemla, and those who refuse to covenant to support a free government are put to death.

l: Christians, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: Christians are the true believers in Christ who belong to the church of God. They gladly take upon themselves the name of Christ, and Moroni prays that their cause and the freedom of the land will be favored.

l: church of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: The church of God is cared for by Helaman and his brethren, who are high priests. Some members are led away by Amalickiah’s flattering words, while Helaman and the high priests later maintain order and experience peace and rejoicing in the church.

l: land of Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: The land of Zarahemla receives the Amalickiahites who are captured and brought back by Moroni’s army.

l: land of Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: The land of Nephi is where Amalickiah and the followers who depart with him go after fearing that he will not gain his desired point.

l: chosen land, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: Moroni names all the land south of the land Desolation, and ultimately all the land on the north and south, a chosen land.

l: land of liberty, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: Moroni names the land a land of liberty and teaches that God will not allow the people who take upon themselves the name of Christ to be destroyed until their own transgressions bring it upon them.

l: title of liberty, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: The title of liberty is made from a rent part of Moroni’s coat and bears the words concerning God, religion, freedom, peace, wives, and children. Moroni raises it before the people, and later causes it to be hoisted upon every tower in the Nephite land.

l: dissensions, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: Dissensions arise when people refuse to hearken to Helaman and his brethren and are led by Amalickiah’s flatteries. They make the affairs of the Nephites precarious and dangerous and cause Moroni to gather forces against Amalickiah.

l: covenant of freedom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: The covenant of freedom requires support for the cause of freedom and a free government. Those who will not enter the covenant are put to death, while only a few deny it.

l: march against Amalickiah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: Moroni takes his gathered and armed army into the wilderness to cut off Amalickiah’s course. He heads Amalickiah’s armies, causing Amalickiah to flee and the remainder of his men to be delivered into Moroni’s hands.

l: peace in the land, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: Peace returns to the land after Moroni establishes the standard of liberty among the Nephites. The people maintain peace until nearly the end of the nineteenth year of the reign of the judges.

l: liberty, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: Freedom is identified with the rights, religion, and free government that the people covenant to maintain. Moroni gathers the people to defend it, and the people believe God will bless them as they uphold it.

l: religion, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: The people covenant to maintain their religion along with their rights. Amalickiah seeks to destroy the religion of the church of God, while Moroni’s title of liberty calls the people to preserve it.

l: faith of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: Those who die in the faith of Christ are described as happy and as having their souls redeemed by the Lord Jesus Christ.

l: wickedness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 46
s: The people covenant that they will not forsake God, and that if they transgress or become ashamed to take upon themselves the name of Christ, the Lord will rend them as they have rent their garments. Moroni teaches that destruction will come upon the people through their own transgressions.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: Amalickiah stirs the Lamanites against the Nephites and schemes to dethrone the king of the Lamanites. He gains control of the armies at Onidah by persuading Lehonti to join forces with him, then causes Lehonti to be poisoned and becomes chief commander. Amalickiah’s servants assassinate the king, and he uses deception to blame the king’s servants before taking possession of the city of Nephi. He marries the queen and becomes king, while the king’s servants flee to Zarahemla and join the people of Ammon.

l: Amalickiah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: Amalickiah stirs the Lamanites to anger against the Nephites and plans to dethrone the king of the Lamanites. He gains command of the armies, causes Lehonti to be poisoned, arranges the king’s assassination, marries the queen, and obtains the kingdom through fraud.

l: Lehonti, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: Lehonti leads the Lamanites who refuse to go against the Nephites and gathers them on mount Antipas. He joins with Amalickiah and becomes a second leader, but Amalickiah causes him to die by poison administered by degrees.

l: king of the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: The king issues a proclamation for his people to gather for battle against the Nephites and gives Amalickiah command over the obedient part of his army. Amalickiah’s servant stabs him to the heart, and Amalickiah falsely blames the king’s servants for his death.

l: queen, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: The queen receives Amalickiah’s message about the king’s death and asks him to spare the city’s people and provide witnesses. Amalickiah wins her favor, marries her, and thereby obtains the kingdom.

l: servants of the king, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: The servants of the king flee after the king is stabbed. Amalickiah falsely accuses them, and they escape into the wilderness, cross into the land of Zarahemla, and join the people of Ammon.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: The Lamanites fear the king’s command to battle the Nephites, and most refuse to obey it. They gather at Onidah and mount Antipas, and later Amalickiah gains their hearts and is acknowledged as their king.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: The Nephites are the people whom the Lamanites are commanded to fight. The king’s servants who flee from Amalickiah cross into the land of Zarahemla and join the people of Ammon.

l: armies of Lehonti, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: The armies of Lehonti surround Amalickiah’s men before dawn after Lehonti agrees to Amalickiah’s plan. They receive Amalickiah’s men after those men plead to join them.

l: army of Amalickiah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: The army of Amalickiah camps near mount Antipas and is initially commanded to compel the disobedient Lamanites to arms. It is surrounded by Lehonti’s armies, joins with them, and later marches with Amalickiah to the land of Nephi and the city of Nephi.

l: armies of the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: The Lamanite armies include those loyal to the king and those gathered under Lehonti at mount Antipas. Amalickiah seeks their favor and ultimately places himself at their head.

l: land of Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: The land of Nephi is where Amalickiah goes among the Lamanites and later marches after gaining command of the armies. He proceeds to the city of Nephi, its chief city.

l: city of Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: The city of Nephi is the chief city in the land of Nephi. Amalickiah enters it with his armies and takes possession of it after the king is assassinated.

l: Onidah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: Onidah is the place where the Lamanites who refuse to fight the Nephites flee. They gather there at the place of arms and appoint a king and leader over themselves.

l: mount Antipas, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: Mount Antipas is where the Lamanites who resist the king gather in preparation for battle. Amalickiah camps in the nearby valley and uses secret messages to negotiate with Lehonti.

l: kingdom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: The kingdom is the power Amalickiah seeks to obtain by dethroning the king. He gains it through the king’s assassination, fraud, and marriage to the queen.

l: proclamation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: The proclamation is sent throughout the Lamanite land by the king, commanding the people to gather again for battle against the Nephites. Most of the people refuse to obey it because they fear losing their lives.

l: war against the Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: The battle against the Nephites is the conflict for which the king commands the Lamanites to gather. The Lamanites fear this battle, and many refuse to participate.

l: dethroning the king, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: Dethroning the king is Amalickiah’s intention from the beginning of his command over the Lamanite army. He accomplishes it by gaining control of the armies and arranging the king’s assassination.

l: death of Lehonti, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: The death of Lehonti is caused by poison that Amalickiah has one of his servants administer by degrees. After Lehonti dies, the Lamanites appoint Amalickiah as their leader and chief commander.

l: king murdered by Amalickiah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: The assassination of the king occurs when one of Amalickiah’s servants stabs him to the heart while appearing to honor him. Amalickiah then uses fraud to accuse the king’s servants and gain the people’s support.

l: marriage of Amalickiah and the queen, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: The marriage of Amalickiah and the queen helps Amalickiah obtain the kingdom. After the marriage, he is acknowledged as king throughout the land among the Lamanites and related groups.

l: fraud, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 47
s: Fraud enables Amalickiah to gain the hearts of the people after the king’s assassination. Through fraud and the assistance of his cunning servants, he obtains the kingdom.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 48
s: Amalickiah becomes king over the Lamanites and stirs them to attack the Nephites, seeking to rule all the land and place the Nephites in bondage. Moroni strengthens the Nephite armies and fortifications while preparing the people to remain faithful to God and defend their liberty, lands, families, and religion. Moroni is described as a mighty, understanding man who dislikes bloodshed and labors for the welfare and safety of his people. Helaman and his brethren preach and baptize, bringing four years of peace among the Nephites before war with the Lamanites resumes.

l: Amalickiah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 48
s: Amalickiah becomes king over the Lamanites, appoints men to stir them against the Nephites, gathers a large army, and seeks to rule all the land and bring the Nephites into bondage.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 48
s: The Lamanites are stirred to anger by Amalickiah and gather to battle against the Nephites. They are led by chief captains appointed from among the Zoramites.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 48
s: The Nephites strengthen their armies and fortifications under Moroni and prepare to defend their land, families, peace, liberty, and religion. They later contend reluctantly with the Lamanites to preserve their lives and families.

l: land, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 48
s: The land is being fortified throughout its cities and borders, especially at its weakest fortifications. Amalickiah seeks to reign over all the land and its people.

l: Moroni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 48
s: Moroni prepares the Nephites to be faithful to God, strengthens their armies, and builds forts, earthworks, and stone walls. He is described as mighty, understanding, opposed to bloodshed, devoted to liberty, and committed to the welfare and safety of his people.

l: liberty, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 48
s: Liberty is something Moroni and the Nephites labor to support and preserve. Moroni's soul rejoices in the liberty and freedom of his country and brethren from bondage and slavery.

l: people of Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 48
s: Moroni's people are strengthened and taught to defend themselves without giving offense. They are taught that God will prosper and deliver them if they keep his commandments.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 48
s: God is described as the source of the Nephites' privileges and blessings and as one who can prosper, warn, direct, and deliver them when they keep his commandments.

l: bondage, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 48
s: Amalickiah seeks to bring the Nephites into bondage. Moroni defends his people and their freedom from bondage and slavery.

l: faith of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 48
s: Moroni is firm in the faith of Christ and swears to defend his people, rights, country, and religion even to the loss of his blood.

l: war, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 48
s: The Nephites are taught to fight only when necessary to preserve their lives, and they are reluctant to shed blood. Despite their reluctance, they are compelled to contend with the Lamanites, and the wars continue for many years.

l: peace, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 48
s: The Nephites enjoy peace and freedom from wars and contentions among themselves for four years because the people humble themselves after the preaching of Helaman and his brethren.

l: commandments of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 48
s: Keeping the commandments of God is taught as the condition for prospering in the land and receiving warning, direction, and deliverance. Moroni's faith centers on keeping the commandments and resisting iniquity.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 49
s: The Lamanites, or Amalickiahites, attacked the Nephite cities of Ammonihah and Noah but were repeatedly repelled by defenses prepared under Moroni’s direction. Moroni stationed an army at Ammonihah, fortified the cities, and appointed Lehi as chief captain over Noah. The Lamanite chief captains were slain, more than a thousand Lamanites were killed, and no Nephites were slain, though about fifty were wounded. The Lamanites fled to inform Amalickiah, who became angry and cursed God and Moroni, while the Nephites thanked the Lord for their deliverance.

l: Moroni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 49
s: Moroni stationed an army by the borders of Ammonihah, raised defensive earthworks, and fortified cities throughout the land. He appointed Lehi as chief captain over Noah, and his preparations enabled the Nephites to defeat the Lamanites.

l: Amalickiah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 49
s: Amalickiah did not come down to battle, and his chief captains did not attack Ammonihah because Moroni had altered the Nephite defenses. After learning of the Lamanites’ losses, Amalickiah became exceedingly angry, cursed God and Moroni, and swore to drink Moroni’s blood.

l: Lehi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 49
s: Lehi was appointed by Moroni as chief captain over the city of Noah. The Lamanites feared Lehi exceedingly when they learned that he commanded the city.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 49
s: The Nephites prepared fortified cities and successfully defended themselves against the Lamanites. They suffered no deaths in the battle, about fifty were wounded, and they thanked the Lord for delivering them.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 49
s: The Lamanites attacked Ammonihah and Noah but could not overcome the Nephite defenses. Their chief captains were slain, more than a thousand Lamanites were killed, and the survivors fled into the wilderness and returned to Nephi.

l: chief captains, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 49
s: The chief captains were astonished by the Nephite preparations but brought their armies against Ammonihah and Noah. They were all slain during the failed attacks.

l: land of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 49
s: The city of Ammonihah had been partly rebuilt after its earlier destruction and was defended by a high ridge of earth and a restricted entrance. The Lamanites expected it to be an easy target but were driven back with great slaughter.

l: city of Noah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 49
s: The city of Noah had previously been weak but was fortified by Moroni until it exceeded the strength of Ammonihah. The Lamanites attacked it through the entrance but were defeated by its defenders.

l: armies of the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 49
s: The armies of the Lamanites approached Ammonihah, retreated to the wilderness, and marched to Noah. They could not breach the Nephite forts and suffered heavy losses before fleeing.

l: Nephite army, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 49
s: The Nephite army was stationed by the borders of Ammonihah to defend the city. Its preparations helped prevent the Lamanites from taking the city.

l: places of security, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 49
s: The forts of security were built or fortified throughout the land under Moroni’s direction. Their high banks, deep ditches, and guarded entrances prevented the Lamanites from entering except through the designated passes.

l: city defenses, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 49
s: The city defenses included raised banks of earth, deep ditches, shields, breastplates, head-plates, swords, slings, stones, and arrows. These defenses gave the Nephites power over the attacking Lamanites.

l: war, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 49
s: The war in this unit involved Lamanite attacks on fortified Nephite cities. The Nephites prevailed because of their preparations and the leadership of Moroni and Lehi.

l: Lamanite attack on Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 49
s: The Lamanite attack on Ammonihah failed because the city had been rebuilt in part and surrounded by strong defenses. The Lamanites were unable to enter except through the guarded entrance and were driven back.

l: Lamanite attack on Noah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 49
s: The Lamanite attack on Noah failed after the Lamanites found that the formerly weak city had been strongly fortified. Their attempts to enter or lower the banks were met with stones and arrows, causing heavy losses.

l: destruction of the Lamanite armies, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 49
s: The Lamanite armies were destroyed in their attacks on the fortified Nephite cities. Their chief captains and more than a thousand Lamanites were slain, while the remaining Lamanites fled into the wilderness.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 50
s: Moroni strengthens Nephite defenses, drives the Lamanites from the east wilderness, establishes armies and cities, and helps the Nephites prosper in peace. A conflict between the people of Lehi and the people of Morianton leads Morianton to flee northward, but Teancum defeats his army and restores peace. Nephihah dies after serving as chief judge, and Pahoran is appointed to the judgment-seat. The unit teaches that the Lord's promises to Lehi are fulfilled as the obedient prosper and the disobedient suffer destruction, bondage, or unbelief.

l: Moroni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 50
s: Moroni directs preparations for war and defense, builds strongholds around the Nephite cities, drives the Lamanites from the east wilderness, establishes armies and cities, and sends Teancum against Morianton. He protects the liberty and peace of the Nephites.

l: Morianton, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 50
s: Morianton leads his people in claiming part of the land of Lehi and taking up arms against them. After angering and beating a maid servant, he plans to flee northward, but Teancum kills him in battle.
